groups.title: Nasal Decongestant Drops
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion caused by sinusitis, allergic rhinitis or a head cold (acute rhinitis).
groups.usage: For adults and children aged 10 years and over, spray 2 to 3 drops into each nostril 1 to 2 times, every 12 hours. For children aged 6 years to under 10 years, spray 2 to 3 drops into each nostril once, every 12 hours. Use for more than 1 week is not recommended, and leave a break of a few days before using it again.
groups.caution: Do not use in people hypersensitive to this medicine, children under 6 years, people with dry rhinitis or glaucoma, people receiving an MAO inhibitor, a tricyclic antidepressant, maprotiline or a blood-pressure-raising medicine, people with difficulty passing urine due to prostate enlargement, people who have had trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy, people with acute coronary artery disease or cardiac asthma, or women who are breastfeeding. Before use, people with coronary heart disease, high blood pressure, hyperthyroidism, metabolic disease or phaeochromocytoma, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not use it together with an MAO inhibitor, a tricyclic antidepressant or maprotiline.

summaryTable.Use: Nasal congestion from sinusitis, allergic rhinitis or a cold
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 years; glaucoma; MAO inhibitor or antidepressant use; breastfeeding

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Gargle
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve inflammation from gingivitis, stomatitis, thrush, before and after tooth extraction, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, and oral mucositis caused by physical factors such as radiotherapy and intubation.
groups.usage: Gargle with 15 mL 2 to 3 times a day, either undiluted or diluted with a small amount of water. Do not use continuously for more than 7 days without the guidance of a doctor. Adjust appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before using this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. Do not use in people hypersensitive to this medicine or in children aged 12 years or under. People hypersensitive to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine) should consult a doctor or pharmacist. After gargling, spit the liquid out and do not use it internally. If you are using an antipyretic analgesic, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Gingivitis, stomatitis, thrush, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, oral mucositis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Children 12 years or under; regular alcohol use; tartrazine sensitivity

groups.title: Children's Nasal Decongestant Spray
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a head cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: For children aged 2 years to under 12 years, spray 1 puff into each nostril 1 to 3 times a day. Leave an interval of at least 8 hours between applications. Do not exceed 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not use in people hypersensitive to this medicine or with such a history, infants under 2 years, people who have had surgery exposing the dura mater or trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy, people with closed-angle glaucoma, dry rhinitis or atrophic rhinitis, phaeochromocytoma or benign prostatic hyperplasia. Before use, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breastfeeding, have a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, migraine or food allergy, have experienced allergic symptoms such as fever, rash, redness, swelling, irritation, joint pain, asthma or itching, or if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, thyroid disease or glaucoma, or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, or a cough lasting or recurring for more than 1 week.

summaryTable.Use: Nasal congestion, runny nose and sneezing in children
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 2 years; glaucoma, heart disease, thyroid disease; pregnancy

groups.title: Hand Antiseptic Solution
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands.
groups.usage: Apply to the hands undiluted, as it is.
groups.caution: Do not use in people hypersensitive to this medicine, and do not use it on mucosal surfaces such as inside the mouth, or on damaged skin and mucous membranes. People hypersensitive to other medicines and people with allergic disease such as asthma, or with such a history or family history, should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Contact with the eyes may damage the cornea, so avoid getting it into the eyes; if it does, wash them out immediately and thoroughly with clean water. Use this medicine undiluted. Do not use it for any purpose other than hand disinfection. It is flammable and volatile, so keep it away from fire. Organic material such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the antiseptic action, so wash these away thoroughly before use.

summaryTable.Use: Hand disinfection
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Damaged skin and mucous membranes; asthma or allergic disease

groups.title: Topical Solution for Corns and Calluses
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for corns and calluses.
groups.usage: After removing the film formed previously, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not use in children under 7 years, in patients being treated for diabetes, or on the face, around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on soft skin areas such as the neck, or on areas with inflammation or wounds. Before use, people hypersensitive to medicines or cosmetics, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and people with diabetes should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Keep to the stated directions and amount. When used for a child, use under the supervision of a guardian. For external use only and do not use it internally. Avoid contact with the eyes; if it gets into the eyes, wash them out immediately with water. If it gets onto healthy skin, that area may turn white, soften and become painful, so take care that it does not touch the skin around the affected area, and wipe it off immediately if it does.

summaryTable.Use: Corns and calluses
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 7 years; diabetes; pregnancy; face, eyes, mucous membranes

groups.title: Hand Antiseptic Solution
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands.
groups.usage: Apply to the hands undiluted, as it is.
groups.caution: Do not use in anyone who has experienced hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine. Do not use it on mucosal surfaces such as inside the mouth, or on damaged skin and mucous membranes. People hypersensitive to other medicines and people with an allergic constitution such as asthma should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Contact with the eyes may damage the cornea, so avoid getting it into the eyes; if it does, wash them out immediately and thoroughly with clean water. Use this medicine undiluted. Do not use it for any purpose other than hand disinfection. Repeated use may make the skin rough through removal of natural oils, so take care. It is flammable and volatile, so keep it well away from fire. Organic material such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the antiseptic action, so wash these away thoroughly before use.

summaryTable.Use: Hand disinfection
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Chlorhexidine sensitivity; damaged skin and mucous membranes

groups.title: Oral Rinse for Mouth Inflammation
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by dentures, oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngitis and aphthous stomatitis, and for sterilisation and disinfection after periodontal membrane surgery.
groups.usage: Rinse the mouth with 15 mL for about 1 minute, 2 times a day. For denture-related stomatitis, soak and clean the denture for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Adjust appropriately according to age and symptoms. Treatment does not normally continue for more than 10 days.
groups.caution: Do not use over a long period because it may upset the normal bacterial balance in the mouth. Do not use in anyone hypersensitive to this medicine. Before use, people with allergic disease such as asthma or with such a history or family history, people wearing anterior prostheses with rough surfaces or gaps, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and children under 18 years should consult a doctor or pharmacist. For ordinary bacterial infection an antibiotic should be given. After treating a patient with both gingivitis and periodontitis, the presence or absence of gingivitis should not be used as an important criterion for judging periodontitis treatment. It may cause staining of oral surfaces such as the tooth surface, prostheses and the back of the tongue. Use only as a mouth rinse and do not use it internally.

summaryTable.Use: Denture inflammation, oral candidiasis, gingivitis, pharyngitis, aphthous stomatitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 18 years; asthma or allergic disease; pregnancy, breastfeeding

groups.title: Nasal Moisturising Spray
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to moisturise and protect the nasal mucosa.
groups.usage: Spray 1 to 2 puffs into the left and right nostril per application, 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not use in anyone hypersensitive to this medicine. Before use, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have another illness. Use this medicine in the nose only; do not use it internally or in the eyes or ears. If you use another product applied to the nose, leave an interval of at least 30 minutes and use this medicine last. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible. When used for a child, use under the supervision of a guardian. Before use, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are using another medicine.

summaryTable.Use: Moisturising and protecting the nasal mucosa
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Other illness or other medicines in use

groups.title: Dry Mouth Spray
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for reduced saliva production caused by medicine treatment, radiotherapy to the mouth or throat area, salivary gland infection, infection of the mouth or throat, dental or oral surgery, fever, or emotional factors.
groups.usage: Spray directly into the mouth or throat 1 to 2 times, as much as is needed to keep the mouth moist or as directed by a doctor.
groups.caution: Do not use in anyone hypersensitive to this medicine. Do not spray into the eyes.

groups.title: Topical Antifungal Cream
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for athlete's foot, tinea cruris (jock itch) and tinea corporis.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 2 to 3 times a day.
groups.caution: Do not use on or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (for example inside the mouth, inside the nose or the vagina), on the genital or vulval area, or on an affected area with severe eczema, weeping, erosion, cracking or injury. People hypersensitive to this medicine or to cosmetics, people with an allergic constitution, people whose affected area is on the face or is widespread, people whose affected area is festering, people for whom the distinction between eczema and tinea is unclear, and infants and young children should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Keep to the stated directions and amount. When used for a child, use under the supervision of a guardian. For external use only and do not use it internally. Take care that it does not get into the eyes. Do not apply directly if the affected area or the surrounding skin is dirty.

summaryTable.Use: Athlete's foot, tinea cruris, tinea corporis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Face or widespread area; festering skin; infants and young children

groups.title: Antiseptic Solution for Hands and Skin
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection for health and hygiene workers and for operators during surgery, and disinfection of the skin at a surgical site), disinfection of medical devices, disinfection of furniture and equipment, and disinfection of wound areas of the skin.
groups.usage: Dilute to the following concentrations according to the purpose. For disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection for health and hygiene workers and for operators during surgery, and disinfection of the skin at a surgical site), use a 0.1 or 0.5% aqueous solution; for disinfection of medical devices, use a 0.1 or 0.5% aqueous solution or a 0.5% ethanol solution; for disinfection of furniture and equipment and for disinfection of wound areas of the skin, use a 0.05% aqueous solution.
groups.caution: Do not use in anyone who has experienced hypersensitivity to this medicine, and do not use it on the brain, spinal cord, ear, or on mucosal surfaces such as the vagina, bladder and mouth, or in the eyes. People hypersensitive to other medicines, people with allergic disease such as asthma or with such a history or family history, and use around the vulva immediately before childbirth should be discussed with a doctor or pharmacist. For external use only; do not use it internally and do not inject it. When using it over a wide area or for a long period, take care not to inhale the vapour. Contact with the eyes may damage the cornea, so avoid getting it into the eyes; if it does, wash them out immediately and thoroughly with clean water. Do not use it for obstetric and gynaecological purposes or for urological purposes. When disinfecting instruments such as syringes and catheters that may touch nerves or mucosal surfaces, use sterile water.

summaryTable.Use: Disinfection of hands, skin, wound areas, medical devices, furniture and equipment
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Asthma or allergic disease; avoid mucous membranes and eyes

groups.title: Skin Antiseptic Solution
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for local disinfection of the skin.
groups.usage: Use undiluted, as it is. Use on clean, dry hands. Wet the hands and nails with this medicine and rub it vigorously over all hand surfaces until dry.
groups.caution: Do not use in anyone hypersensitive to this medicine. Do not use it for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on the brain, spinal cord, eyes, mucous membranes (especially genital mucosa), or in the auditory canal when the eardrum is perforated. Before use, consult a doctor or pharmacist when applying it to broken skin (especially burns) or to a large area of immature skin. For external use only; do not swallow it and do not inject it. It is a flammable liquid, so take care. Because of the risk of burns, let it dry before using electrical equipment. Do not use this medicine together with or immediately after soap, as the action may be inhibited or inactivated. Do not use it with detergents or other chemicals.

summaryTable.Use: Local disinfection of the skin
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Broken skin or burns; large-area use; flammable - keep from fire
